title: Per-question correct counts behind the figures and tables of the paper

format.file: counts.jsonl: one JSON object per line, one per (benchmark, model, question, setting)

keys.id: question id: LiveCodeBench question_id, MATH-500 unique_id, Hi-ToM s<sample_id>_o<question_order>_<prompting_type>
keys.temperature: sampling temperature tau (for a min_p sweep, its fixed tau)
keys.min_p: min_p value; null for the temperature sweeps (0.0 inside a min_p sweep is plain sampling)
keys.n: number of samples (question_n parse: the question-level n, see n_cell)
keys.n_cell: optional, question_n files only: the cell's own sample count where it differs from n

format.setting: the temperature for a temperature sweep, the min_p value for a min_p sweep
format.populations: every file holds every question the paper's analysis code read for that study, in that order; 'included' is the subset its inclusion rule keeps (the analyses apply the rule themselves; included_ids.json lists it for checking)
format.question_order: each use records the order its analysis read the questions in: 'file' (the file's own order, that of the source the paper's code loaded) or 'sorted ids' (the ids sorted as strings, which is how the Appendix I comparisons, profiles, hardness, KL and protection analyses read the min_p and Hi-ToM questions); seeded draws, splits and tie breaks follow that order

included.rule: fitted peak >= 0.1 %: the degree-10 Bernstein profile fit of the question's counts peaks at a pass rate of at least 1e-3 (the paper's filter), on this file's question_n counts

files.question_order: as the paper's analysis code read the source file
files.samples: ~1.5k per cell, harder questions ~10k (Qwen3-0.6B: about doubled on some hard questions)
